title: The River Crossing
text_content: During the holiday, Obi and his cousin Nneka visited their grandfather's village beside a wide river. Every morning, Grandpa Ike fished from a wooden canoe while the children collected firewood. One afternoon, heavy clouds gathered and the river began to rise much faster than anyone had expected. Obi realised that the old wooden bridge to the farm would soon disappear under the brown water. Grandpa Ike was still working on the far side and did not know about the dangerous situation. Nneka wanted to run across immediately, but Obi held her arm and told her to think carefully first. They remembered the old canoe by the bank and decided to paddle across before the water rose higher. Obi steered while Nneka paddled, and the strong current pushed them steadily downstream. In the middle of the river, an enormous log struck the canoe, and cold water splashed over the side. Nneka stayed very calm, picked up a small bucket and began to scoop out the water. At last the canoe touched the muddy bank, and Obi ran to warn his grandfather about the flood. Grandpa Ike hurried back with them, carrying his tools and a basket of fresh vegetables. That evening everyone agreed that the children had been clever and brave, and Obi felt proud.
